articles.headline: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, top pick, more
articles.description: ESPN's Football Power Index projects the 2027 NFL draft order for Round 1, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.
articles.body:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

See more on the NFL draft

First-round picks that have been traded:

The Green Bay Packers' selection was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys in the Micah Parsons trade.

The Indianapolis Colts' selection was dealt to the New York Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade.

The Los Angeles Rams' selection was dealt to the Cleveland Browns in the Myles Garrett trade.

The better of Dallas' two selections (either its own pick or the Packers' original pick) was dealt to the Jets in the Quinnen Williams trade.

articles.headline: 2026 NFL playoff picture: AFC, NFC seed projections, chances
articles.description: We're looking ahead to how the 14-team playoff picture could line up -- and who will win divisions -- en route to the Super Bowl.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is underway, and while it's still very early, we're already starting to track the playoff picture and the road to Super Bowl LXI. Which teams have the best chances to make the 14-team postseason field? Which have a lot of work to do to ultimately get in?

We used ESPN's Football Power Index to project the rest of the season, looking at the playoff picture for both conferences. We included updated odds for every team to make the postseason, clinch its division and even make the Super Bowl in February. Plus, we also have the FPI's projections for every game on the upcoming slate and how a win -- or a loss -- might impact each team's playoff chances, independent of other results.

Here's everything you need to know about the playoff picture right now.

articles.headline: Van Ness' breakout game saves Packers in OT win vs. Jets
articles.description: Packers hope it's a sign of things to come as Micah Parsons nears his return from a torn ACL.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- No one was more excited about what Lukas Van Ness did in Sunday's 20-17 overtime win against the New York Jets than Micah Parsons -- to the point that Parsons was telling some of his fellow Green Bay Packers defensive players that Van Ness was so dominant at the line of scrimmage that he should never, ever drop into coverage.

And the more Parsons talked in the back corner of the locker room, the louder he got.

After all, Parsons has been touting the underachieving Van Ness ever since he arrived in Green Bay last year. This offseason, he predicted the defensive end would break out and said Van Ness' popularity might rival his own.

Parsons, who has at least two more weeks on the physically unable to perform list before he can come back from last year's torn ACL, might have some catching up to do after a game like this from Van Ness: nine tackles (three for a loss), 1.5 sacks and four quarterback hits.

The Packers needed every bit of it to come back from a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit and beat the Jets in overtime at MetLife Stadium on a day when injuries piled up, especially on offense.

While Parsons slipped out the back door without talking to reporters, there were plenty of others left to sing Van Ness' praises.

"He was all over the place," coach Matt LaFleur said.

"It seemed like he was everywhere," Packers safety Evan Williams said.

"He was flying around making a lot of plays, especially at the end," quarterback Jordan Love said.

The end was when they needed it the most.

How about a fourth-and-1 stuff of running back Braelon Allen at midfield with the game tied and 1:15 left in regulation? It got the Packers to overtime.

And what about a shared sack with rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton on the Jets' second play of overtime right after Barryn Sorrell and Brandon Cisse sacked Geno Smith on the first play? Next thing you know, the Jets were in third-and-30 and punting the ball away to set up Trey Smack's game-winning field goal.

"I was just focused on dominating," said Van Ness, whose status for the game was unclear until Saturday when he passed the concussion protocol.

To be sure, there were other standout defensive plays by other players. There was Williams' breakup of a deep pass intended for receiver Adonai Mitchell right before the 2-minute warning in the fourth quarter. There was safety Xavier McKinney's tackle on third down to stop a drive and force a punt that Skyy Moore returned 63 yards to set up the game-tying field goal with 2:59 left in regulation. And there was coordinator Jonathan Gannon seemingly knowing exactly when to send pressure.

"I can't give enough credit to our defense, our defensive staff, Jonathan Gannon, just calling a very aggressive game," LaFleur said. "I'm sure glad we got him because I think he's an elite defensive coordinator, football coach and just a great leader."

articles.headline: Donald in, Garrett out: How will Rams defense look with huge addition (and subtraction)?
articles.description: Despite the defensive tackle returning from retirement, L.A. has never doubted that he could still make an impact.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- When Aaron Donald runs onto the field at SoFi Stadium on Monday night, it will have been 981 days since he last played in an NFL game.

Though the future Pro Football Hall of Fame defensive tackle said he knows it has been two full seasons since he walked off the field after the season-ending loss to the Detroit Lions, in a way, it feels like he never left.

"[After] being back around, I feel like I was just here last year," Donald said. "Time flies by so fast, and I forget that I haven't play[ed] football for two years. I feel like I'm just back to my normal self."

Donald did not play in -- or even travel to -- the Rams' season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia, as he worked to get up to speed after coming out of retirement Aug. 30.

He began thinking about rejoining the Rams after hearing from coach Sean McVay in late May that Los Angeles was considering trading for reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett. In the past three years, the Rams had built "a stacked" defensive line, Donald said, but when the Rams traded for Garrett on June 1, Donald started to think about how much fun he might have playing with the group.

Donald's return to the field Monday night against the New York Giants (8:15 ET, ESPN) will look slightly different than he and the team expected. A week ago, Garrett had arthroscopic surgery on his knee, requiring a trip to the injured reserve list that will keep the pass rusher sidelined for at least the next four games. Though McVay said Garrett's absence is unrelated to how the Rams will handle Donald's return, there's no doubt not having the pass rusher on the field -- despite the outstanding pass-rush group around him -- impacts Donald.

Instead of the chance to play with a player who might be double-teamed, giving him the chance to face more single coverage than he did throughout his career, Donald will likely be getting the extra attention from teams, even if he hasn't played in two seasons.

Despite Donald not playing in 2024 or '25, he ranks second in pass rush wins since 2017, according to ESPN Analytics/NFL Next Gen Stats. He had that success even though he was double-teamed on the fourth-most pass rush plays in the NFL over that span. His 276 pass rush wins against double-teams are still by far the most in the league since 2017, when pass rush win rate was first tracked.

Though Donald laughed off the idea of being double- or triple-teamed after coming out of retirement -- "They ain't worried about me, man!" -- McVay said he believes the Rams will see Donald playing at the same level he did before he retired.

In early September, 49ers left tackle Trent Williams described going against Donald as "trying to catch a fish in water with your bare hands."

"I expect him to be the same [No.] 99 that the league grew to fear," Williams said.

articles.headline: Carragher questions Wirtz future in Liverpool XI after latest struggles
articles.description: Jamie Carragher has called on Andoni Iraola to drop Florian Wirtz for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City after describing the midfielder's display against Bournemouth as one of his worst since arriving at Anfield.
articles.headlineJa: キャラガー、最近の不振を受けヴィルツのリヴァプールでの先発定着に疑問符
articles.descriptionJa: ジェイミー・キャラガーは、ボーンマス戦でのフロリアン・ヴィルツのパフォーマンスをアンフィールド加入以来最悪の部類と評し、マンチェスター・シティ戦に向けてアンドニ・イラオラに同MFを外すよう求めました。
articles.body:
Jamie Carragher has called on Andoni Iraola to drop Florian Wirtz for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City after describing the midfielder's display against Bournemouth as one of his worst since arriving at Anfield.

Wirtz struggled to make an impact in Liverpool's 1-0 win at the Vitality Stadium, prompting Carragher to question whether his underwhelming start is simply a matter of form or a sign of a bigger problem.

"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," Carragher said on the Jamie Carragher Podcast.

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy, he keeps possession, there's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.

"But the reason I worry is, I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is."

Carragher had already voiced his frustration with Wirtz while on commentary during the game, saying of his first-half display, "It's just nothing. Nothing is happening there at all."

The former Liverpool defender said his concerns over Wirtz predated Saturday's performance and pointed to a previous game against Burnley as an example of the lack of attacking threat he believes the midfielder has shown.

"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game it was what I've seen for the last 12 months: I don't see how he's going to hurt you. It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid."

Wirtz arrived at Liverpool amid significant expectations, but Carragher believes the midfielder has considerable ground to make up if he is to become the player the club expected.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

"The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting."

Carragher also believes Wirtz's role at No. 10 is forcing Szoboszlai into a position that does not suit him.

"And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player, I don't."

articles.headline: Man United's Michael Carrick concerned about Benjamin Sesko's latest injury
articles.description: Michael Carrick has raised concerns about Benjamin Sesko's latest injury by revealing the problem is connected to the same shin issue which kept the striker sidelined for more than two months over the summer.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのマイケル・キャリック、ベンヤミン・シェシュコの最新の負傷に懸念
articles.descriptionJa: マイケル・キャリックは、ベンヤミン・シェシュコの最新の負傷について、夏に同ストライカーを2か月以上離脱させたのと同じすねの問題に関連していることを明かし、懸念を示しました。
articles.body:
Michael Carrick has raised concerns about Benjamin Sesko's latest injury by revealing the problem is connected to the same shin issue which kept the striker sidelined for more than two months over the summer.

Sesko missed the final three games of last season with the injury which also prevented the 23-year-old from taking part in any of United's preseason fixtures.

He returned as a substitute on the opening weekend against Hull, one of six appearances in all competitions he's made this season.

But after starting the 3-2 Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton on Wednesday, Sesko was absent from the squad against Fulham on Sunday.

And afterwards Carrick revealed the Slovenian is suffering from recurrence of the same shin problem.

"We're not sure with Ben yet," the United head coach said.

"He felt a bit of pain after the game [against Brighton] so we're assessing him. At the moment, he definitely wasn't ready for [Fulham], so I haven't really got any more news to give you at this point. We'll have to see what that brings."

- Cole Palmer withdraws from England's Nations League squad - sources

- Michael Carrick keen to find Man United positives, but there aren't many right now

Carrick will hope that the extended international break gives some of his injured players time to get back to full fitness.

Summer signing Carlos Baleba was on the bench for the first time at Craven Cottage while Matthijs de Ligt made the trip to London, but wasn't fit enough to be named in the squad.

Winger Amad Diallo is yet to play this season. Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo were both named in the England squad, but ongoing issues may mean they are forced to pull out.

articles.headline: Dodgers get better of Giants' bullpen in 3-1 win to sweep three-game series
articles.description: — Kiké Hernández hit a go-ahead RBI double in the seventh inning, Emmet Sheehan did not give up a run in 5 1/3 innings, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 3-1 on Sunday to complete a three-game sweep.
articles.headlineJa: ドジャースが3-1でジャイアンツのブルペン陣を攻略、3連戦をスイープ
articles.descriptionJa: キケ・ヘルナンデスが7回に勝ち越しの適時二塁打を放ち、エメット・シーハンが5回1/3を無失点に抑え、ロサンゼルス・ドジャースが日曜日にサンフランシスコ・ジャイアンツを3-1で破り3連戦スイープを達成しました。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — Kiké Hernández hit a go-ahead RBI double in the seventh inning, Emmet Sheehan did not give up a run in 5 1/3 innings, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 3-1 on Sunday to complete a three-game sweep.


              Hernández jumped on the first pitch he saw from Sam Hentges (1-7), driving in Max Muncy to put the Dodgers ahead 2-1. Muncy pushed an insurance run across with a single in the eighth.


              Kris Bubic (4-2) pitched 2/3 of an inning for the win, and Tanner Scott handled the ninth inning for his 23rd save.


              Sheehan made the most of a bullpen game to strengthen his credentials for making the Dodgers’ postseason roster as a long reliever. He had nine strikeouts against one hit and one walk after taking over from Jack Dreyer in the second inning.


              Matt Wilkinson allowed three hits and no walks while striking out six in five scoreless innings, but the Giants’ bullpen buckled. The 23-year-old left-hander was acquired as part of the trade that sent catcher Patrick Bailey to Cleveland in May.


              Tommy Edman homered to right in the sixth inning to tie the game at 1, tagging reliever Carson Seymour for the 400-foot shot.


              Jonah Cox drew a leadoff walk to help spot the Giants their 1-0 lead. Cox reached second on a bad pickoff attempt by Dreyer before stealing third, and Victor Bericoto’s single drove him home.


              Up next
              Giants: RHP Blade Tidwell (1-2, 4.56 ERA) starts in the opener of a three-game series against the Minnesota Twins on Monday night, facing RHP Bailey Ober (7-6, 4.32).


              Dodgers: Manager Dave Roberts said there would be another bullpen game Tuesday night to start a three-game series against the San Diego Padres, who have yet to set their rotation.

articles.headline: Why this 3-week international break is longest ever (and why that's a good thing)
articles.description: Fans have grown used to international games interrupting the club season, but this break will be a week longer than before. It's not as bad as it sounds.
articles.headlineJa: 今回の3週間にわたる代表ウィークが過去最長となる理由（そしてそれが良いことである理由）
articles.descriptionJa: ファンはクラブのシーズンが代表戦で中断することに慣れてきていますが、今回のブレイクはこれまでより1週間長くなります。とはいえ、聞いたほど悪いことではありません。
articles.body:
It feels like the new club season has only just begun, and yet we are already having to reckon with the prospect of 2026-27's first international break.

While fans have grown used to matches between national teams providing an early interruption just a few weeks into the campaign, there will be something different about the upcoming round of men's international fixtures: It will be a week longer.

While that may sound like a terrifying prospect to many a fan hooked on the top club competitions such as the UEFA Champions League, Premier League and LaLiga, the situation is not as bad as it sounds. That's because this break is the first to fall under FIFA's reconfigured international match calendar.

- 2026 Ballon d'Or: Full men's, women's shortlists, host city, more

- USMNT's gifted next generation kick-start road to 2030 World Cup

- Messi's emotional Argentina farewell shows he hasn't forgotten criticism

Previously, in the first half of each season there were three separate two-game international breaks held in September, October and November every year, with another the following March. But to minimize disruption to the domestic club schedule across the men's and women's game, FIFA voted unanimously to approve changes to its calendar in 2023. The 2026-27 season will be the first to see these alterations come into effect.

As such, we will now see an extended, 16-day international break taking place between Sept. 21 and Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6) that will allow national teams to fit four matches into one window. This reduces the number of international breaks in the first half of the season from three to two, and limits the total number of weeks that club seasons are put on hold reduced from six to five.

From now on, there will be only three international breaks a season that fall during the domestic campaign. This season, they are as follows:

1. Sept. 21-Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6)

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

As per FIFA's updated calendar, the fourth and fifth international breaks of the season come in June and July, once the club season is over. That allows room in the itinerary for international tournaments to take place during a period when most club leagues around the world are not active. For example, the finals of the Concacaf Gold Cup, CAF Africa Cup of Nations and UEFA Nations League will all be held next summer. The one exception to this is the AFC Asian Cup, which will take place in Saudi Arabia next year between Jan. 7 and Feb. 5.

While the changes to the international calendar will certainly have an impact when it comes to limiting the disruption to the domestic season, they don't go far enough for Arsène Wenger, FIFA's chief of global football development.
